name: Italy
note: Family members (or the hospital) must declare a death to the comune's civil status officer within 24 hours, and an ASL-appointed medico necroscopo must verify the death before burial is authorised. The comune records the death in ANPR, the national population register that has replaced municipal registers and that public administrations read automatically. INPS is told twice, by the medico necroscopo within 48 hours and by the comune within two days, and passes the death to every pension payer. The private sector has no general death feed.

steps.title: The medico necroscopo verifies the death and certifies it
steps.who: The medico necroscopo appointed by the local health unit (in hospitals, the medical director or a delegate).

deadline.text: not earlier than 15 and not later than 30 hours after the death

steps.summary: An ASL-appointed doctor, independent of the treating doctor outside hospitals, examines the body and certifies the death; the civil status officer may not authorise burial until death has been verified this way.

steps.title: Treating doctor reports the cause of death to the mayor on the ISTAT death form
steps.localName: denuncia della causa di morte; scheda ISTAT
steps.who: The doctor who attended the deceased; for a death without medical care, the medico necroscopo; also doctors performing judicial or diagnostic autopsies.

deadline.text: within 24 hours of verification of the death

steps.summary: The cause of death is reported to the mayor (the comune, which is also the civil status office) on the death form set by the Ministry of Health with ISTAT. The form serves health, epidemiological and statistical purposes only.

steps.title: Suspected crime is reported to the public prosecutor, whose clearance gates burial
steps.who: The civil status officer (or the mayor for cremation) who finds signs of a crime; the procuratore della Repubblica.
steps.trigger: Signs or suspicion of violent death or of death due to a crime.
steps.summary: The officer must report to the public prosecutor at once. Burial, entombment or cremation cannot be authorised until a magistrate or judicial police officer, assisted by a doctor, has examined the body, and the judicial authority's clearance is presented.

steps.title: Family declares the death to the civil status officer within 24 hours
steps.who: One of the relatives, a person living with the deceased, or their delegate; failing them, anyone informed of the death.
steps.summary: The declaration goes to the civil status officer of the place of death; it may also be made in digital form by certified e-mail (PEC).

steps.title: Hospital or institution sends a notice of death, which can be digital
steps.who: The director of the hospital, nursing or care home, or other institution, or a delegate.
steps.summary: The institution must send the notice within the same 24 hours, electronically if drawn up digitally; the officer may draw up the death record from a digital notice sent by the health authority.

steps.title: Civil status officer authorises burial or cremation
steps.who: The civil status officer of the comune where the death occurred; the authorisation goes to those entitled or the funeral firm and cemetery operators.
steps.trigger: Verification of death by the medico necroscopo and receipt of the death notice, ISTAT form and certificates.

deadline.text: not before 24 hours from the death

steps.summary: No burial without the officer's prior authorisation, which cannot be given before 24 hours have passed and death has been verified; documents may be sent by PEC.

steps.title: Extracts of the death record
steps.who: Anyone for a summary extract; a full copy only to a person with an interest.
steps.summary: Civil status registers are public and officers must issue the extracts and certificates requested. Summary extracts are the norm; full copies require an express request by someone with an interest.

steps.title: The death is recorded in ANPR, the national resident population register
steps.who: The comune, as civil status and registry office, working in ANPR, which replaces municipal population registers and holds the national civil status archive.
steps.summary: ANPR, kept at the Ministry of the Interior, has replaced the municipal population registers and contains the national computerised archive of civil status registers, so the comune's entry is the national record.

steps.title: Public administrations read ANPR or keep their files aligned with it
steps.who: Public administrations and public-service operators, including the Agenzia delle Entrate, through the national data interoperability platform.
steps.summary: Administrations access ANPR data automatically through the PDND platform, and must use ANPR exclusively or keep their own files constantly aligned with it.

steps.title: Medico necroscopo sends the death certificate to INPS
steps.summary: The certificate of verification of death goes online to INPS within 48 hours; breach carries administrative penalties.

steps.title: Comuni notify INPS of deaths within two days

deadline.text: within two days of the event

steps.summary: INPS provides comuni with an electronic channel for deaths, which they must use within two days; delay causing loss exposes the responsible official to liability.

steps.title: INPS passes the comuni's death data to all pension payers
steps.who: INPS, through the Casellario delle pensioni, to the bodies that pay pensions.
steps.summary: Using the central pensions register, INPS forwards the information received from the comuni to every pension-paying body.

steps.title: Comune sends a copy of the death form to the local health unit
steps.who: The comune where the death occurred, to its local health unit (and on to the unit of residence).
steps.summary: Each local health unit keeps a register of deaths and causes for each comune.

steps.title: The ISTAT death form reaches the national statistics institute
steps.summary: The cause-of-death form is designed with ISTAT and serves statistical purposes; the provision for its onward transmission to ISTAT was not located.

steps.title: Deceased electors are struck from the electoral lists
steps.who: The comune's electoral officer and commission.
steps.trigger: Death, proved by an authentic document.

deadline.text: no later than the fifteenth day before an election

steps.summary: Death is one of the few grounds on which the electoral lists may be changed between half-yearly revisions.

steps.title: Pensions paid into a bank after death must be returned to INPS
steps.who: Banks and Poste italiane holding the account; INPS or INAIL request return.
steps.trigger: A benefit credited for a period after the death.
steps.summary: Benefits paid after the death are credited subject to reserve; the bank must return them from the available balance and may not use them to recover its own debts.

steps.title: Comuni may let entitled bodies use ANPR registry data
steps.who: Persons entitled to the data, through the PDND platform or specific agreements (convenzioni) with the comune.
steps.summary: There is no general death feed to banks or insurers in the CAD; access for non-public bodies depends on entitlement and an agreement.

registrationDeadlineDays.note: The declaration (or the institution's notice) is due within 24 hours of the death.

informantDuty.note: Relatives, a cohabitant or their delegate (failing them anyone informed) declare the death; hospitals and other institutions must send a notice of death.

medicalExaminerScrutiny.note: No independent review of cause-of-death certificates. Every death is verified before burial by a medico necroscopo appointed by the local health unit, but that confirms the fact of death, not the certified cause.

electronicRegistration.note: The declaration may be made by PEC and the health authority may transmit a digital notice from which the death record is drawn up; paper remains possible.

governmentPropagation.note: ANPR is read by administrations automatically; INPS is told by the medico necroscopo within 48 hours and by the comune within two days, and passes the death to all pension payers.

certificateAccess.note: Registers are public and summary extracts are issued on request; a full copy needs an express request from someone with an interest.

privateSectorVerification.note: No general death-data service for the private sector; comuni can allow entitled parties to use ANPR data through the PDND platform or agreements. Banks hear of deaths from INPS when it reclaims post-death pension payments.

gaps: The provision requiring onward transmission of the ISTAT death form to ISTAT was not located; the it-istat step is unverified.
Art. 31, c. 19 L. 289/2002: its first period (comuni to INPS) was suppressed by D.L. 112/2008, whose art. 20, c. 12 now sets the two-day duty; only the surviving second period (Casellario) is cited.
Whether CAD art. 2, c. 2, lett. b (public-service operators) brings private companies within automatic ANPR access was not checked; art. 2 was not read.
No specific provision found on a death feed to the Agenzia delle Entrate beyond the general ANPR alignment duty in CAD art. 62, c. 5; the it-pa step targets the tax authority on that general basis.
